Subject: Blue pills going round Levy — please read this properly, and talk to your kids this week

I've just come off nights so I'll keep this as clear as I can.

The police warning is up on this board somewhere, but nobody's reading it, and the thread about Saturday has turned into rumours and people having a go at kids. So I'm putting this up as its own post. I'd rather be the annoying one banging on than read about another young person in a bad way.

The tablets are blue and they're being sold as diazepam or "Xanax". Some of them have nitazenes in them — synthetic opioids that are far stronger than heroin. That's not me exaggerating for effect, that's what's in them. You cannot tell by looking at them, and neither can the person selling them. A tablet that looks exactly like the last one you took can be a completely different strength.

The signs to watch for: extreme drowsiness, pinpoint pupils, slow or noisy breathing, blue lips. If you see any of that, or they won't wake up properly, it is 999 straight away. Not in a bit. Not after you've had a think about it.

And this is the bit I really need people to hear. Do not put them to bed to sleep it off. Do not leave them and ring for help hours later. By the time you ring, the brain has been without oxygen far too long, and that damage is done. I'm not saying that to frighten anyone for the sake of it, I'm saying it because it's the difference between someone coming home and someone not. The other thing that stops people ringing is worrying about getting in trouble. So — the police have said it themselves, plainly, their priority is preserving life. Ringing 999 is the right thing to do, full stop. Nobody is going to be more worried about the paperwork than about your mate breathing.

If you want to be able to do something while you wait, naloxone nasal spray reverses opioids. You can get it free from Brightpath, the drug and alcohol service on Stockport Road, next to the launderette. Anyone can ask. No names needed, no referral, nothing like that. The training takes about ten minutes. They're open Monday to Friday, 10 till 4, and Thursday until 7. If you've got a kid who's out and about, or you're out yourself, it's worth knowing where that is.

Parents — please talk to your kids about this this week. Not after half term, not when it comes up, this week. I had the chat with my lad, who's 14, over his tea last night. Eye rolls, obviously. But he listened, and he asked me what pinpoint pupils meant, and that's exactly the point — he now knows what to look for and that he can ring me. Awkward ten minutes is nothing.

And can we stop with the comments about the kids. Slagging them off helps nobody. Scared kids don't ring for help, and that is the whole problem in the first place.

Please share this rather than just liking it — share it to your own page, into your family group chat, wherever it'll actually be seen. That's what makes the difference.

Becky
